# driver

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/driver"
```

Package driver owns module compilation.

A module is the unit of compilation because imports, build constraints, and test packages decide which files form a program. The driver keeps those choices consistent across frontend checking and lowering. It uses Go's build rules so TGo files belong to the same packages as their Go equivalents.

Source files are authoritative. Existing generated files can be stale and must not affect source checking. The driver first writes original TGo at generated paths, then replaces it with checked generated Go.

Compilation passes data through these steps: read module files, prepare a generated Go paths, select source with Go's build rules, check source packages, lower expressions, check emitted Go, and collect output. Each step keeps the data required by the next step.

The driver returns the emitted module as file contents. The caller can write output elsewhere. Expression evaluation rules belong to the lowerer.

## func Compile

```go
func Compile(dir string) map[string][]byte
```

Compile translates the module's TGo files and returns file contents by module\-relative path. It writes generated Go into the module, keeps other files in the result, and panics on failure.
